title: Set Pieces & Restarts
description: Corners, free kicks, penalties, throw-ins, and restart decisions.

questions.question: On a throw-in, what should the thrower look for first?
options: A teammate who is open and ready
The longest throw possible
A teammate marked tightly
The most crowded central space
questions.explanation: The best throw-in keeps the ball with your team, even if it is short.

questions.question: In the diagram, which throw-in option is usually safest if A is open to feet?
options: Throw to A's feet
Force it into the crowded middle
Throw toward a marked teammate
Wait until the open lane closes
questions.explanation: A short open option helps your team keep possession and play forward after receiving.

questions.question: At the moment you release a throw-in, what must your feet do?
options: Keep part of each foot touching the line or the ground outside it
Have both feet entirely inside the field
Lift one foot to add distance
Jump with both feet before releasing
questions.explanation: Some part of each foot must stay on the touchline or the ground behind it at release. You also face the field and throw with both hands from behind and over your head.

questions.question: Under standard offside rules, can you be penalized for receiving directly from a throw-in in an offside position?
options: No, a direct throw-in reception is an exception
Yes, if you receive in the attacking half
Yes, unless a defender touches it first
Only if the throw goes backward
questions.explanation: There is no offside offence for receiving directly from a throw-in. After a teammate next plays the ball, ordinary offside decisions can apply.

questions.question: On an attacking corner, what should players do before the kick?
options: Know their run or job
All attack the exact same space
Wait flat-footed until the ball arrives
Stand behind the keeper before the kick
questions.explanation: Good corners work best when each player knows where to run and who attacks rebounds.

questions.question: In the corner diagram, why is the player at the edge of the box useful?
questions.imageAlt: Corner kick with near post, spot, and edge options
options: They can shoot or stop a clearance
They should stand on the goal line
They make the near-post run crowded
They mark their own teammate
questions.explanation: The edge player can win loose clearances and help stop counter-attacks.

questions.question: When defending a corner, what matters most?
options: Mark players, protect space, and be first to the ball
All chase the kicker
Stand still
Wait for the keeper to do everything
questions.explanation: Corners are dangerous, so defenders must communicate and attack the ball.

questions.question: What does a direct free kick allow?
options: A goal straight into the opponents' goal without another player touching it
A goal only after a second teammate touches it
The kicker to play the ball twice before anyone else
The ball to be kicked while rolling
questions.explanation: A direct free kick can go straight into the opponents' goal. You can still choose a pass when it offers a better chance.

questions.question: In the direct free kick diagram, what should the shooter consider before shooting?
questions.imageAlt: Direct free kick with wall and passing option
options: Distance, wall, keeper, and a possible pass
Only how hard they can kick
Only the nearest defender
Whether every teammate is inside the wall
questions.explanation: A smart free kick choice depends on the whole picture, not just power.

questions.question: How can an indirect free kick lead to a goal?
options: The ball must touch another player before entering the goal
The kicker can kick it twice themselves
The ball only needs to touch a post first
It counts directly if the kick is powerful enough
questions.explanation: Another player, a teammate or opponent, must touch the ball. The referee signals an indirect free kick with a raised arm.

questions.question: In the indirect free-kick diagram, what makes the planned second player's shot valid?
questions.imageAlt: Indirect free kick with first touch and shot
options: The first player kicks the ball so it clearly moves, then the second plays it
The first player rests a foot on a ball that stays still
The first player takes two touches before the second
The second player shoots before the first touch
questions.explanation: The restart must put the ball into play with clear movement. The second player then provides the other touch needed for a goal.

questions.question: What should the defending team do on a free kick near their goal?
options: Set a wall, mark runners, and listen to the keeper
All run to midfield and leave the box open
Turn away from the shooter
Stand behind the goal line
questions.explanation: The wall blocks the shot, while other defenders mark passes and rebounds.

questions.question: On a penalty kick, what should the shooter focus on?
options: Pick a spot, stay calm, and strike cleanly
Change their mind during the run-up
Strike without looking at the ball
Aim at the keeper's body
questions.explanation: A calm, clean strike gives the shooter the best chance.

questions.question: During normal play, your penalty is saved and the ball stays loose. What can you do?
options: Try for the rebound after the keeper has touched it
Touch it again even if it only hit the post
Kick it out of the keeper's hands
Stop because penalty rebounds never count
questions.explanation: In normal play, the taker may play the ball again after another player touches it. A post alone does not count. Penalty shoot-outs do not allow follow-up shots.

questions.question: On a goal kick, what is a good team shape?
options: Spread out to create safe passing lanes
All stand in one corner
Stay behind opponents
Stand flat on the goal line
questions.explanation: Good spacing gives the kicker more safe choices.

questions.question: A quick free kick may help your team. What should you check first?
options: The ball is stationary, the option is useful, and the referee has not told you to wait
Only whether the other team is distracted
Whether you can move the ball to a better place
Whether your teammate will notice after you kick
questions.explanation: A quick restart still needs to follow the rules. If the referee requires a whistle, wait for it.

questions.question: The referee tells you to wait for the whistle before a free kick. What should you do?
options: Wait for the whistle
Kick as soon as a teammate calls
Kick if a defender looks away
Move closer to goal before taking it
questions.explanation: Follow the referee's instruction. Taking it too early can lead to a retake and a caution.

questions.question: What is a good job for a player not attacking the ball on a corner?
options: Stay balanced to stop a counter-attack
Stand beyond the far sideline
Watch without marking anyone
Crowd the shooter at the corner
questions.explanation: Not everyone should crash the goal; some players protect the team if the ball is cleared.

questions.question: When the other team has a throw-in, what should nearby defenders do?
options: Track receivers and close passing lanes while respecting the thrower's space
Stand against the thrower to block their arms
Leave every receiver free and watch the ball
Turn away until the throw is taken
questions.explanation: Mark and communicate without obstructing the throw. Under standard Laws, opponents must stay at least two metres from the throw-in point.

questions.question: Why are set pieces important?
options: They are planned chances to score or defend well
They rarely affect field position
They are only for goalkeepers
They remove the need for teamwork
questions.explanation: Restarts happen every game, and a prepared team can gain a big advantage.

questions.question: Your team has an attacking corner. An opponent stays high for a counter. What job is useful away from the goalmouth?
options: Cover the outlet and be ready for a clearance
Add another runner into the same crowded goalmouth
Stand beside the corner taker with no passing lane
Watch from the halfway line without checking the opponent
questions.explanation: A set piece includes both the scoring chance and what happens if possession changes. Balance the attack with players ready to protect the team.

questions.question: Under standard Laws in normal play, your penalty hits only the post and rebounds to you. What should you do?
options: Let another player touch it before you play it again
Shoot again immediately because the post resets the play
Pick up the ball and ask to retake the kick
Dribble once before taking a second shot
questions.explanation: The taker cannot touch the ball again until it touches another player. The post or crossbar is not another player.

questions.question: A short corner draws two defenders out. A teammate is now open in a better crossing position. What is the purpose of the short combination?
options: Change the angle and create a better delivery opportunity
Use extra passes even if the original cross was clear
Remove the need for runners in the penalty area
Keep the ball by the corner for the entire attack
questions.explanation: A short corner can move defenders and open another angle. Read the response; if it closes down, keep the ball through another safe option.

questions.question: A defender follows your first movement at a throw-in. How can you create a new receiving lane?
options: Change direction and time the next movement with the thrower
Hold the same position and ask for a harder throw
Push the marker away before receiving
Move into the lane a teammate is already using
questions.explanation: A change of direction can separate you from a marker. Coordinate with the thrower so the lane is open when the ball is released.

questions.question: The referee signals an indirect free kick near goal. The defense expects a short touch then a shot. What should your team still read?
options: The wall, the open lanes, and whether a pass creates a better chance
Only the original plan, regardless of the defense
Only which teammate can kick hardest
Only whether the ball is close enough for a direct shot
questions.explanation: A restart plan is a starting point. The required touches still apply, but a different combination may work better if opponents block the planned route.
